items.title: Malaysia's Shariah-Compliant Bitcoin ETF Milestone
points: Halogen Shariah Bitcoin ETF approved by Malaysian regulators and set to debut December 2 on Bursa Malaysia, the country's main stock exchange.
First-ever Bitcoin ETF (exchange-traded fund—a fund tracking an asset that trades on stock exchanges) to meet Shariah compliance standards, expanding crypto access to Muslim-majority markets.
Demonstrates growing institutional and regulatory acceptance of Bitcoin across geographies and religious frameworks.

items.title: Abraxas Capital Bitcoin Purchase
points: Abraxas Capital purchased 21,520 bitcoin worth $1.28 billion this week, signaling continued institutional demand for digital assets.

items.title: Bitcoin Options Expiry & Downside Hedging Surge
points: $6.8 billion in Bitcoin options expired on Deribit Friday, clearing roughly 25% of the exchange's outstanding positions.

Traders have shifted significantly toward downside protection since October, with substantial put (a contract giving the right to sell at a set price) positions concentrated at $40,000—nearly half won't expire until Christmas Day.
Another major expiry of approximately 165,000 BTC (roughly $10 billion notional value) falls due on December 25, suggesting prolonged price pressure ahead.
Bitcoin's drop below $59,000 on Friday, combined with a bearish death cross technical pattern, indicates weakening momentum despite Thanksgiving stability.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETF Outflows Signal Investor Retreat
points: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced their worst month on record since launching, with $5.4B in redemptions during November.
The outflows coincide with options traders' defensive positioning, suggesting institutional and retail investors are both reducing exposure.
Combined with derivatives hedging, the dual pressure—both from options markets and direct ETF redemptions—indicates widespread concern about further downside.

items.title: Binance Hack Recovery & Operations Restoration
points: Binance fully lifted withdrawal suspensions four weeks after October's $6.4 billion hack, restoring normal operations.
U.S. authorities have assisted in freezing, seizing, or returning $2.9 billion of the stolen funds, though the majority remains unrecovered.
The recovery milestone helps restore confidence in the exchange but underscores the scale of losses still at large.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam Upgrade Date Set
points: Ethereum developers locked in December 15 as the date for the Glamsterdam upgrade's contested gas changes (adjustments to the fees paid for processing transactions).
The date follows security concerns that halted a prior fork (a software upgrade splitting from the previous protocol version) attempt in October.
